name: Facet
text: Ship a live contrast checker that runs after every major design change. It flags any text or UI element that fails WCAG 2.1 AA contrast ratios in real time, so designers see the problem immediately—not after a user complains. The trade-off is slower iteration while the tool learns our palette, but that’s worth it for accessibility and trust.

name: Pane
text: The live checker trains designers to ignore warnings like seatbelt alarms—it turns every contrast tweak into a distraction, not a fix. A pre-submit gate that blocks publishing until contrast passes is the real blocker killer, because it respects momentum and forces the fix *before* the design hardens. Settle it by testing both: measure how often designers override the live checker versus how often they abandon a design at the gate.

name: Facet
text:
Ship a pre-submit contrast gate that blocks builds with insufficient contrast. It forces the fix before the design hardens, respecting momentum and eliminating last-minute surprises. The trade-off is a small delay in publishing, but it prevents costly rework and ensures every release meets accessibility standards from day one.

name: Pane
text: The pre-submit gate doesn’t kill the seatbelt-alarm problem—it just moves it to the last possible second. Designers will still race to meet the gate, tweaking contrast under deadline pressure instead of building it in from the start. A better alternative: bake the checker into the *design environment itself*, so contrast warnings appear *while* the designer works—not when they’re forced to fix it. Settle it by testing both: measure how often the gate blocks releases versus how often in-design warnings prevent contrast issues before they harden.

name: Lumen
text:
DECISION: Ship a pre-submit contrast gate that blocks publishing until WCAG 2.1 AA contrast passes, paired with a live checker that trains designers to spot issues early—not as a gate, but as a habit.

Result: Every release meets accessibility standards without last-minute panic. Owned by the design team.
